section_summary: These pages trace Japanese wartime labor mobilization, including student and women workers, military control of essential workers, and attempts to maintain production. They also contain U.S. planning for occupation labor policy and the opening portion of a Foreign Economic Administration report on industrial safety, hygiene, discipline, and protections for women and children.

subfiles.title: Economic Press - Japan
subfiles.about: Reports press accounts of Japanese labor mobilization and industrial labor and electricity shortages in occupied China.
subfiles.summary: Press extracts describe expanded student and women labor mobilization, declining labor migration to Manchukuo, and Shanghai factory electricity allotments.

subfiles.title: Labor Policy of Military Government in Japan
subfiles.about: Reviews draft occupation labor policy and proposes language encouraging the use of labor organizations.
subfiles.summary: Sullivan compares draft and revised policy language on unions, collective bargaining, social services, and labor recruitment.

subfiles.title: The Civilian Volunteer Combat Corps as an Instrument of Labor Control
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japan’s Combat Corps as a means of imposing military discipline on essential wartime workers.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues that the corps principally serves labor control, despite its stated combat purpose. It describes railway mobilization and proposed aircraft and road-transport units, then examines worker resistance, absenteeism, and government pressure for stricter controls.

subfiles.title: Japan: Current Emergency Labor Control Measures
subfiles.about: Summarizes new controls over skilled workers, seamen, regional labor administration, and railway workers.
subfiles.summary: Reports technician task units, a naval shipping corps, decentralized labor powers, and the Railway Combat Corps inauguration.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Two FEA Reports
subfiles.from: Constance G. Gaynor, Chief, Project Control Staff
subfiles.to: E. B. Lyon, Foreign Activity Correlation, State Department
subfiles.about: Forwards reports on Japanese working conditions and administration of Imperial Household property.
subfiles.summary: Forwards copies of two Foreign Economic Administration reports.

subfiles.title: Working Conditions Other Than Wages and Hours in Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses Japanese industrial safety, hygiene, and discipline and recommends occupation measures.
subfiles.summary: The report surveys prewar protections and wartime deterioration in factories, dormitories, mines, and the merchant marine. It recommends restoring and enforcing selected prewar standards, repealing repressive discipline laws, and supporting worker organization. These pages also examine protections for women and begin the discussion of child labor.
